# MLP encoder migration requirements

- Preserve the original frozen C `mlp_encoder` behavior as the migration reference. Its SHA256 is `ECE6D0A8033A26E2528042A7B74C66C249EA3C8D7378C06809FB94C8F6BD79B8`. The user authorized retiring the C sources and binaries after validation; their historical versions remain in Git. Optional differential tests require an explicitly supplied external oracle with this hash. Do not replace or modify an external oracle, or restore a C dependency to default Rust builds.
- Translate the C implementation function by function into Rust. Preserve corresponding function boundaries, state structures, parameter semantics, branch and loop ordering, arithmetic and rounding, candidate ordering, tie-breaking, and serialization behavior. Adapt syntax and ownership for Rust without substituting a different algorithm.
- Preserve the call relationships between corresponding functions. Do not merge functions, reorganize the call graph, or introduce an independently designed encoding pipeline in place of the C implementation.
- When changing migrated encoding behavior, compare the corresponding C implementation from Git history with Rust function by function and check their call relationships, in addition to applicable tests and integration checks.
- With identical PCM, encoding parameters, and explicit metadata, retain byte-for-byte and raw SHA256 comparison. On 2026-10-14 the user additionally authorized excluding machine/time auxiliary identification metadata when comparing default outputs: use the documented `mlp-coded-v1-no-auxiliary-stamp` SHA256 scheme, which excludes the first directory stamp bit and its dependent parity bit only after validating original header parity. Report this as coded-stream equality, not raw-file equality; the entire auxiliary identification stream is excluded. Decoded PCM equality is not an acceptance substitute. See `docs/MLP-PARITY.md`.
- Do not patch encoded output or call the C encoder in the Rust production implementation to manufacture parity. Read-only, in-memory normalization is permitted only for the comparison scheme above. C reference adapters and explicit original metadata replay are permitted only for testing; production generates its own identity/time metadata by default.
- Report remaining differences honestly. Do not declare migration complete or release the Rust encoder until the strict acceptance above passes. Do not commit, push, replace tags, or publish without renewed user authorization.
